pages.title: Magnetizer
pages.text: A coil around an iron core that pulses a field through a magnet blank. Only a field stronger than the blank's coercivity sets it.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Its coil gives 0.6 T; each iron block or magnetic block touching it adds 0.35 T. A Ferrite Magnet needs 0.35 T, a $(item)Neodymium Magnet$() 1.2 T (two touching blocks), a $(item)Samarium-Cobalt Magnet$() 2.0 T (four).
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 1 fluid inputs, 1 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Ferrite Magnet, Neodymium Magnet, Samarium-Cobalt Magnet.
The strongest permanent magnet known: a thumb-sized piece can hold a kilogram of steel. Loses its strength above about 80 °C.$(br2)Made in $(item)Magnetizer$().
A little weaker than neodymium, but it keeps its field up to 300 °C - the magnet for hot machines.$(br2)Made in $(item)Pulsed Magnet Lab$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Neodymium Magnet$(): Bending Magnet, Central Solenoid, Centrifuge Rotor, Condensate Trap, Disk Confinement Ring and more
